chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Dawud al-Raqqi said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever buys a beast of burden, its back belongs to him, and its provision is upon Allah.'

key_terms.دَابَّةٌ: Beast of burden or animal used for riding/carrying loads
key_terms.ظَهْرُهَا: Its back (referring to the right to ride or load it)

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of an owner regarding a purchased animal's usage and sustenance in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on tethering horses, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the division of rights between the owner and the Divine. It establishes that while the physical utility of the animal belongs to the purchaser, its sustenance is divinely provided, reinforcing the Shia legal principle that ownership entails responsibility for upkeep while acknowledging Allah as the ultimate Provider (Ar-Razzaq).
